decision: Force the headless OpenCV 4.x wheel on every platform in tools/venv.sh, and assert cv2.__version__ starts with 4.
why: rapidocr pulls an unpinned opencv-python that wins the cv2 import over homr's pinned headless <5; the swap existed but was guarded by uname = Linux.
evidence: venv held opencv-python 5.0.0.93 and opencv-python-headless 4.14.0.94 at once.
result: Applied. cv2 is now 4.14.0 and rapidocr still imports.

decision: Do not re-dump the golden fixtures.
why: OpenCV 4.14.0 and 5.0.0 agree on minAreaRect and boxPoints, and the checked-in boxes-*.json reproduce byte for byte under 4.14.0 including the -45 entries.
evidence: Raw minAreaRect and boxPoints on boxes-stems_rest idx 0 and 96 matched the stored box and polygon exactly.
result: Fixtures kept. 42 files untouched.

decision: Convert every raw opencv.js rect to opencv-python's [-90, 0) convention before homr's normalisation, by subtracting 90 and swapping w/h while the angle is >= 0.
why: opencv.js 4.12.0 uses the post-4.5.1 (0, 90] convention; opencv-python 4.14.0 uses the pre-4.5.1 one. Normalisation absorbs the difference everywhere except exactly +-45, where homr's comparisons are strict.
evidence: 86 of 717 rotated-box entries disagreed in angle sign before the conversion and 0 after; bar_lines went to 103/103 exact on both rect and polygon.
result: Adopted as the design.

decision: Widen the golden box tolerance to cover the angle at 1e-3, not just centres and sizes.
why: Python stores the rect as float32 and the port recomputes in float64.
evidence: Worst observed angle delta 7.7e-7, worst centre/size delta 2.4e-4 across 967 entries.
result: testing.md needs the note; cause identified as required.

decision: Accept that box polygons are not bit-exact, and measure rather than tolerate.
why: The rect differs by ~1e-4 between the two builds, which flips a corner across an integer boundary.
evidence: 18 of 967 entries differ by one pixel on one corner. trunc, floor and an fround pass score identically; round scores worse; a hand-rolled float32 boxPoints matched 0 of 967.
result: Use cv.boxPoints on the converted rect. Downstream merge risk recorded, resolvable only once the merge runs.

decision: Build noteheads through minAreaRect over the concatenated contours, not fitEllipse.
why: _get_ellipse_for_whole_group refits with minAreaRect and every box reaches it, singleton groups included; fitEllipse only gates the 5-point minimum and shapes the polygon the overlap test reads.
evidence: Per-entry fitEllipse diverged in the centre; the minAreaRect route gave 81/81 at 2.4e-4 with no angle mismatch.
result: Adopted.

decision: Scope phase 4 to the five predict_symbols box lists plus prepare_bar_line_image, and leave staff_fragments-broken to phase 5.
why: break_wide_fragments is staff_detection.py, a phase-5 module; the five lists are reproducible from the dumped mask-filtered-*.png alone.
evidence: dump-golden.py writes mask-filtered-* after filter_predictions and make_lines_stronger, so no phase-5 code is needed for the five.
result: Adopted. brace_dot testable but empty on this page.

decision: Do not convert a fitEllipse rect; convert only minAreaRect.
why: The two producers sit in different conventions. fitEllipse agrees bit for bit across opencv.js 4.12.0 and opencv-python 4.14.0; minAreaRect does not.
evidence: 81 of 81 noteheads, worst delta exactly 0 on centre, size and angle. Angle range 10.761 to 67.928, consistent with [0,180) in both.
result: Fork 1 resolved: two producer-specific brands, not one raw-rect type.

decision: Correction: both max_size filters use or, and the real asymmetry is the > 0 per-dimension guard, present on boxes and absent on ellipses.
why: An earlier version of the findings document said the ellipse filter used and. Read from source lines 360-440.
evidence: create_bounding_ellipses has no > 0 guard, so max_size=(100,-1) would reject every ellipse rather than disable the height check.
result: Findings document corrected. Candidate B found this.

decision: Correction: there is a sixth call shape, brace_dot with max_size=(100,-1), and it is the only one exercising the disable rule.
why: The findings document claimed five call shapes and that the rule might be trimmed.
evidence: main.py:280 / dump-golden.py:187.
result: Findings document corrected. Candidate A found this.

decision: No runtime range check on toLegacyAngleConvention; the two producer brands are the whole guard.
why: The while-loop is total: an angle already in [-90, 0) makes zero iterations and passes through unchanged, so a range check would refuse a correct pre-4.5.1 result rather than catch a mislabel. Candidate A wanted the check because its legacyRectOf took the producer as a string argument, which the brands replace.
evidence: Probed @techstark/opencv-js 4.12.0 directly: minAreaRect on a 20x10 axis-aligned contour answers angle +90, size (10, 20), which the loop turns into -90 with the size unchanged, matching what the findings record for opencv-python.
result: Applied. The brands make a wrong conversion a compile error; no throw exists.

decision: axisBoxOf narrows from RotatedBox | Ellipse to RotatedBox.
why: to_bounding_box is defined on RotatedBoundingBox, not on AngledBoundingBox, so no Ellipse ever reaches it in homr. Phase 1's wider signature let one.
evidence: bounding_boxes.py lines 299-309; grep found the method on no other class.
result: Applied. Candidate B's finding about already-shipped code.

decision: Phase 4's new modules take kebab-case filenames (mat-plane.ts, box-merge.ts, ...), not the camelCase the design packages wrote.
why: biome's useFilenamingConvention is an error in this repo and both candidate designs named files in camelCase, so their literal names do not pass npm run lint.
evidence: npx biome check refused src/cv/matPlane.ts and matPoints.ts by name; the existing tree is all kebab-case (default-source.ts).
result: Applied. src/cv/boxes.ts also became src/cv/create-boxes.ts, so no two modules share the basename boxes.ts.

decision: UnionFind stays private to box-merge.ts; mergeOverlappingGroups takes items and a predicate, not groups.
why: Python's groups list is never mutated, so _do_groups_overlap always compares the original singletons and reduces to one predicate call per pair. Exporting the union-find would be a second surface with no caller.
evidence: The non-ascending-root case is reachable through the predicate alone, so nothing needs a hand-made union sequence to pin the Map contract.
result: Applied. Candidate B's collapse, and the module imports no cv.

decision: OverlapTester.overlaps / .overlapsAny replace free isOverlapping / isOverlappingWithAny functions rather than sitting beside them.
why: The synthesis takes the tester from candidate A, and it is the same relation: a second one-shot pair would be two names for one behaviour with no caller until phase 5, and the one-shot is the shape A measured as unusable in the merge.
evidence: Candidate A measured roughly 75 000 Mat allocations per page for the one-Mat-per-comparison form; the test asserts 4 keeps across 6 comparisons.
result: Applied. Phase 5 constructs a tester per loop, which is the shape it wants anyway.

decision: Use homr's own names for the per-box operations (makeBoxThicker, makeBoxTaller, ...) rather than the synthesis's prose names (thicker, taller).
why: Fork 3 settles the *typing* -- kind-preserving through a generic, kind-collapsing by return type -- and fork 2 puts the module in candidate B's map, whose whole naming convention mirrors the Python. createRotatedBoundingBoxes, doPolygonsOverlap and predictSymbols all read that way, so one file naming differently would be the odd one out.
evidence: No measurement; a naming call, recorded because the synthesis writes the other names.
result: Applied.

decision: makeBoxThicker keeps RotatedBoundingBox's `thickness <= 0` early return for ellipses too, which BoundingEllipse does not have.
why: The ellipse override has no guard, so a non-positive thickness there rebuilds the polygon from the normalised rect instead of leaving it alone -- a real difference, but unreachable: the three call sites pass 15, 30 and a positive tolerance, and thicken_boxes is never given a value.
evidence: grep of the whole homr package for make_box_thicker: note_detection.py:131 (15), brace_dot_detection.py:53/72/91, bounding_boxes.py:385 (thicken_boxes, never passed).
result: Applied, with the asymmetry named in the doc comment. Branching on kind would reintroduce the isinstance chain fork 3 removes, for dead code.

decision: No toBoundingBox alias beside axisBoxOf.
why: Candidate B proposed one so the exported name matches Python's, but every other name in the phase is already the camelCase equivalent rather than a transliteration, and axisBoxOf shipped in phase 1.
evidence: None needed; it is one name for one function either way.
result: Not applied.

decision: polygonViaBoxPoints takes no MatScope, where candidate B's sketch does.
why: cv.boxPoints hands back a plain JavaScript array of {x, y} and allocates no Mat, so a scope parameter would be a lie about what the function owns. Candidate A's sketch already had it right.
evidence: Probed directly on 4.12.0: boxPoints accepts a plain rect literal and returns Array.isArray === true with no delete().
result: Applied. polygonViaEllipse2Poly does take one, because its seventh argument must be a PointVector.

decision: Correction: reimplement boxPoints in float32 from OpenCV's direct four-corner formula instead of calling cv.boxPoints, reversing the 2026-09-28 row above.
why: opencv.js 4.12.0's boxPoints reflects the third and fourth corners through the centre where opencv-python 4.14.0 derives all four, so on a bit-identical rect the reflection lands on an integer that the direct form lands 3e-5 below and int() differs by one. Three staff_fragments entries hit it with a bit-exact stored rect, which the synthesis's fork 4 tolerance cannot admit and must not be widened to.
evidence: Over the 595 of 634 rotated golden entries whose raw minAreaRect is bit-identical between the builds: cv.boxPoints equals the reflecting formula 595/595, the direct formula equals opencv-python's floats 595/595, cv.boxPoints equals opencv-python's floats 591/595.
result: Applied. staff_fragments goes 144 to 147 of 147 polygons exact and fork 4 stays as settled. boxPoints left REQUIRED_MEMBERS; the earlier row's "matched 0 of 967" is retracted in phase-4-findings.md.

decision: Drop candidate A's FittedShape wrapper and its float outline; the fitters return plain RotatedBox[] and Ellipse[].
why: It existed only to carry the pre-truncation float so the golden test could derive a per-box corner bound. The synthesis's fork 4 dropped that bound, and the direct boxPoints formula removes the last case that needed one, so the wrapper and shapesOf would be a parameter with no reader.
evidence: Every polygon of the five lists is now exact but one, whose rect is inexact, so the rect-conditioned rule is sufficient.
result: Applied.

decision: predictSymbols takes SegmentationMasks, not InputPredictions.
why: predict_symbols reads only the five masks off its InputPredictions; taking the whole thing would be a parameter the function never looks at.
result: Applied. Candidate B's signature.

decision: Do not port _merge_groups_recursive or BoundingBox's image helpers (extract, blank_everything_outside_of_box, increase_size_in_each_dimension).
why: _merge_groups_recursive is dead code -- defined and never called anywhere in the homr package -- so a port of it could be verified against no fixture and no call site. The three BoundingBox helpers are image cropping, need image_utils.crop_image which is not ported, and have no caller before phase 5.
evidence: grep across the whole homr package for each name.
result: Not ported. Candidate B found the dead merge.

decision: Fork 1, staff-line types: plain readonly objects in src/geometry/, each beside its algorithm (staff-lines.ts, staff-anchors.ts, raw-staffs.ts). FiveLines is a 5-tuple, RawStaff has a box rather than being one, and fragment identity is the rectKey set.
why: Python compares fragments by value (AngledBoundingBox.__eq__ is box equality), so a set of rect keys is the same relation. A RawStaff that is a RotatedBox would be accepted wherever a fragment is.
evidence: The 340 broken Kesh fragments have 340 distinct rects and 147 distinct debug ids, so the debug id is not an identity and the rect is.
result: Adopted from candidate A. docs/design/phase-5-synthesis.md.

decision: Fork 2, numerics: sum, mean, std and floorDiv change in place in src/image/numeric.ts, and npArgsort is a literal aquicksort in src/image/argsort.ts.
why: They are documented as np.sum and friends and are left folds, which differ from numpy from 8 values up. A second pairwise set beside them would leave a wrong default under the right name.
evidence: Candidate A's bodies against numpy 2.5.3: sum, mean and std 880 of 880 arrays, npArgsort 2750 of 2750, floorDiv 4000 of 4000 where Math.floor(a / b) is wrong on 21.
result: Adopted. Both candidates agree. Stage 2 of the build order.

decision: Fork 3, errors: one DetectionError with four codes, thrown. The two upstream IndexError sites throw where Python crashes, and phase 9 turns the throw into { ok: false }.
why: A result union would split failure handling between two mechanisms inside one pipeline and make every stage test unwrap.
evidence: staff_detection.py:572 (peaks[0] on a zone with no peak) and model.py:277 (grid[0] of an empty merge). test/golden/vectors/line-groups.json and staff-merge.json hold both as IndexError.
result: Adopted from candidate A.

decision: Fork 4, preprocessed: PageDetection.preprocessed is the masked page, as upstream, and PageDetection.noise is a three-way outcome (clean, masked, skipped).
why: filter_predictions masks every array including preprocessed when the filter fires, and phase 6 dewarps out of that image. The filter also has a silent mode where more than half the tiles are noisy and nothing is masked.
evidence: noise_filtering.py:94-120. Both public fixtures are clean (0 of 420 tiles), so the other two outcomes are held by test/golden/vectors/noise.json.
result: Adopted from candidate A.

decision: Fork 5, oracle: dump-golden.py unrolls homr functions with a self-check and writes the intermediates, dump-vectors.py writes eleven vector files, and a typeset grand-staff page is a second public fixture.
why: The only public fixture had no brace, no grand staff, no noise mask, no split notehead and no merged staff. Unrolling saves intermediates without patching homr, and the self-check keeps the unrolled copy from drifting.
evidence: Stage 1 built it. The self-checks pass on both fixtures and two runs of each tool write identical bytes.
result: Adopted from candidate A. The rows below record what stage 1 changed.

decision: Fork 6, mutation: none. addNotesToStaffs returns { notes, staffs } and Staff.symbols becomes readonly.
why: A staff that changes under a test that captured it before the notes stage is the aliasing the dumper already works around by ordering its writes.
evidence: note_detection.py:180 (staff.add_symbol). dump-golden.py writes staffs.json before add_notes_to_staffs for this reason.
result: Adopted. Both candidates agree.

decision: Fork 7, modules: candidate A's module map, and src/index.ts keeps one export * per module.
why: BoxOps keeps the ordering and tie logic in src/geometry/ with no cv handle, where candidate B moved seven algorithm files into src/cv/ only because they ask an overlap question.
evidence: The module map is the Modules section of docs/design/phase-5-synthesis.md. Candidate A's sketch type-checked over a copy of the repository under its strict settings.
result: Adopted from candidate A.

decision: Graft from candidate B: the heapsort fallback of npArgsort is never shipped unverified. It is built, and argsort.json tests it.
why: The synthesis allowed the fallback to throw a NumericError only if no input could reach it. Stage 1 built that input, so the throw is not needed.
evidence: McIlroy's adversary played against a transcription of aquicksort in tools/dump-vectors.py. On the input of 200 values numpy heapsorts 170 of them, and on the input of 1000 it heapsorts 962. The transcription with numpy's aheapsort equals np.argsort on both and on the 70 tied and random cases.
result: argsort.json carries both inputs with a heapsorted count. The dumper exits non-zero if an adversarial input stops reaching heapsort.

decision: Graft from candidate B, and a correction: get_staff_for_anchor is a subset test per line index, not a shared fragment on any line.
why: The findings said a staff matched when any one of its five lines shared fragments with the anchor. The code returns the first staff where, for some line index i, the anchor line's fragment set is a subset of the staff's line i.
evidence: staff_detection.py:172-178.
result: docs/design/phase-5-findings.md is corrected in three places. Candidate B found it.

decision: Graft from candidate B: the piano page is committed only if its dump shows a non-empty boxes-brace_dot.json and is_grandstaff true. The page itself is candidate A's four systems.
why: A grand-staff fixture on which homr sees no grand staff covers nothing it was added for. Four systems give detect_staff eight staffs, the smallest count at which np.average in filter_edge_of_vision sums pairwise.
evidence: See the fixture row below for what the dump shows.
result: Gate applied and passed.

decision: Rejected: candidate B's degrade-and-log at the two crash sites.
why: A dropped staff produces a page no golden can check, and the browser would answer where the server fails.
evidence: Python raises at both sites, so there is no Python output to compare a degraded page with.
result: Not adopted. The port throws.

decision: Rejected: candidate B's synthetic mask pages (a generator, a dumper branch, eight golden directories).
why: The vectors call the same Python functions on hand-built inputs at a fraction of the weight. The cost is that vectors skip the box-fitting path, which phase 4's goldens already cover.
evidence: test/golden/vectors/ is 1.0 MB for eleven files. test/golden/grand-staff-300dpi/, one real page, is 6.9 MB.
result: Not adopted.

decision: Rejected: candidate B's Fragment{id, box} interning.
why: An integer id is identity and Python's sets use value equality. The two differ on two fragments with equal rects.
evidence: bounding_boxes.py:179-186 (__eq__ and __hash__ on box).
result: Not adopted.

decision: Rejected: candidate B's PageDetection.log and log-detect.txt.
why: Whether RecognizeResult.log carries homr's stderr is phase 9's question. Phase 5 adds no log.
evidence: None needed.
result: Not adopted.

decision: Rejected: candidate B's restricted src/index.ts and its staffLinePolylines helper.
why: A restricted index breaks the convention of phases 1 to 4 for no caller. The bench reads staff.grid directly, as candidate A's call site does.
evidence: src/index.ts holds one export * per module in every phase so far.
result: Not adopted.

decision: The dumper unrolls four functions, not the two the module map names: create_noise_grid and add_notes_to_staffs join detect_staff and find_braces_brackets_and_grand_staff_lines.
why: noise.json needs the grid and the counts, which create_noise_grid returns to nobody, and notehead-splits.json needs the pieces at the point add_notes_to_staffs calls split_clumps_of_noteheads. Each of the four is followed by the real function and a comparison.
evidence: The four self-checks pass on both fixtures. unrolled_add_notes leaves out staff.add_symbol, so it does not change the staffs the real call then fills.
result: Applied. The shapes of the seven new page files are as in the module map.

decision: The new decoders return plain Golden* shapes (GoldenStaffAnchor, GoldenRawStaff), not StaffAnchor and RawStaff.
why: Those types belong to the stages that port their constructors. A decoder that built them would fix their shape before the code that derives their fields exists.
evidence: The decoder still asserts what it can without the port: five lines per anchor, minY and maxY from the fragment rects, zone as int(minY - 5 units) and int(maxY + 5 units), every index in range, every deduplicated staff either resampled or dropped.
result: Applied. The stage that ports createStaffAnchor may change decodeStaffAnchors to build with it.

decision: Second public fixture kept: test/fixtures/grand-staff-300dpi.png, sixteen bars for piano written for this repository, four systems of two braced staffs.
why: homr sees the abcjs brace on the first attempt, so no bracket or heavier brace was tried.
evidence: Its dump has 25 brace_dot boxes, of which the four braces are 28 px wide and 283 to 288 px tall. All four MultiStaffs hold one staff with is_grandstaff true. 8 staffs, 168 of 169 anchors kept, 102 notes, noise clean.
result: Kept. Typeset by abcjs 6.6.4 in a standalone page and captured by a headless browser, not through the app's PDF export; SOURCE.md says so and holds the ABC.

decision: The piano page shows two noteheads the phase 4 port gets wrong, and they are pinned as known divergences in test/boxes-golden.test.ts rather than fixed or tolerated.
why: opencv.js 4.12.0's minAreaRect returns a rotated rect on the contours of noteheads 18 and 48 where opencv-python 4.14.0 returns the upright one. That is phase 4's code and a new cause, so stage 1 neither widens the tolerance nor changes the port.
evidence: noteheads[18]: Python 22 by 18 at angle 0, the port off by 1.33 px in size and 45 degrees. noteheads[48]: Python 22 by 17 at angle 0, the port off by 2.60 px and 26.6 degrees. The other 100 noteheads and all 832 boxes of the other four lists match.
result: Open. KNOWN_DIVERGENCES names the two entries and the test fails if either starts to match, so a fix removes the entry.

decision: Three committed Kesh files are OpenCV 5.0.0 output and the pinned 4.14.0 does not reproduce them: canvas-1.png, tokens-1.json and voices.json. They are left as committed and not re-dumped in stage 1.
why: The 2026-09-28 row kept the fixtures after checking the box files only. The dewarp of staff 1 differs between the two builds, and the tokens of that staff follow it. Re-dumping changes phase 6 to 8 goldens, which is not stage 1's call.
evidence: The unmodified dumper under 4.14.0 writes a canvas-1.png that differs in 1397 pixels by at most 3 grey levels, all inside x 1118 to 1255 and y 96 to 156, and tokens that differ in coordinates only. Four runs agree. The same dumper with opencv-python 5.0.0.93 on PYTHONPATH reproduces all 42 committed files byte for byte.
result: Open. Every run of npm run golden rewrites those three files, and meta.json's new oracle block says 4.14.0 for a directory that holds three 5.0.0 files. The other 39 files are byte-identical under both builds.

decision: A 15-line staff merge is not in staff-merge.json.
why: Python's Staff.merge accepts a ten-line staff and a five-line one, but _merge_selected_pairs only ever merges two neighbouring five-line staffs, and the port's StaffPoint is 5 or 10 lines by type.
evidence: model.py:498-509. used_staff_index in _select_grandstaffs keeps any staff out of two pairs.
result: Left out. A vector the pipeline cannot reach would ask the model type to admit a state it excludes.

decision: np.argsort's tie order and the noise grid's float-to-uint8 cast are the oracle machine's, and meta.json and every vector file record the machine.
why: numpy ships SIMD argsorts for x86 whose tie order was not compared, and a cast of a float above 255 to uint8 is not defined by C. The expected values are data, so the tests are the same on any machine; what an x86 oracle could change is the dump.
evidence: On arm64 a checkerboard tile's estimate of 2040 is stored as 248, which is 2040 mod 256. noise.json in the vectors holds that case.
result: Recorded. oracle.machine is arm64 in both fixtures and in the eleven vector files.

decision: sum, mean and std are numpy's pairwise reduction in place, and the only caller that passes 8 or more values is createStaffPoint on a ten-line point.
why: The synthesis rested on no phase 1 to 4 caller passing 8 values. That held until stage 1 added a grand-staff fixture, whose merged points have 9 gaps.
evidence: grep over src, bench and tools: mean is called by createStaffPoint (4 gaps, or 9 on a ten-line point) and by decodeStaff's check of it; sum and std had no caller outside numeric.ts. The old left fold is wrong on 36 of the 57 arrays of pairwise.json for sum, 35 for mean and 24 for std, all with 8 or more values.
result: Applied. All 57 arrays are exact for the three functions. No golden moved: the left fold already equalled Python's stored average_unit_size on all 1080 ten-line points of the grand-staff page and on the 19 of staff-merge.json, so those points pass with either sum and only pairwise.json tells the two apart.

decision: floorDiv is CPython's float_floor_div in place, and pySliceBounds returns an empty slice as stop equal to start.
why: Math.floor(a / b) is one too high where the division rounds up to an integer. A caller of pySliceBounds wants a row count, and Python's own slice.indices answers (9, 2) for [-1:2] of 10, which is not one.
evidence: floor-div.json: 434 pairs exact, where Math.floor(a / b) is wrong on 6 (0.5 // 0.1 is 4, and five pairs with a subnormal numerator). The existing callers divide by 2 and by 20 and get the same number as before.
result: Applied. The suite of phases 1 to 4 passes unchanged.

decision: npArgsort ships with numpy's heapsort fallback, and FindPeaksOptions has three optional fields where the sketch required all three.
why: find_peaks takes None for each filter and find-peaks.json calls it that way, so required fields could not drive 39 of its 60 cases. homr's one call passes all three and loses nothing.
evidence: argsort.json: 72 arrays exact, the two adversarial ones included (170 of 200 and 962 of 1000 elements heapsorted). find-peaks.json: 60 cases exact, the largest with 38 peaks.
result: Applied. Deviation from candidate A's sketch, which also left the fallback as a throw.

decision: The move leaves no src/geometry/barlines.ts until the stage that ports detect_bar_lines, and box-fitting.ts keeps its private rotatedBoxOf beside the new rotatedBoxFromRect.
why: A module with no export cannot be re-exported from src/index.ts. rotatedBoxFromRect is the same five lines as rotatedBoxOf, and box-fitting.ts is frozen to an import change while its minAreaRect divergence is diagnosed.
evidence: A script moved the eight functions and compared each with HEAD: 15 of 15 function texts in the four files are identical, doc comments included. No name exported before is missing after (352 before, 405 now). The biome override rejects a file under src/geometry/ that imports ../cv/opencv.js and passes once it is removed.
result: Applied. Fold rotatedBoxOf into rotatedBoxFromRect when box-fitting.ts is open again.

decision: BoxOps keeps one output Mat for every intersects of a scope and one outline Mat per box compared.
why: rotatedRectangleIntersection needs an output Mat per call in opencv.js, and a stage asks tens of thousands of times.
evidence: intersections.json through opencv.js 4.12.0: the raw code equals cv2's on 313 of 313 pairs and isIntersecting equals is_intersecting on 313 of 313, touching pairs included. One scope that pairs noteheads with stems, filters the bar lines and asks 37 400 intersects holds 581 Mats on Kesh; the same on the grand-staff page, 79 937 intersects, holds 728. The intersects add none.
result: Applied. The one-scope-per-stage estimate of 1500 Mats stands; detect.ts still owes the whole-page number.

decision: makeLinesStronger and prepareBraceDotImage take no kernel parameter and are exact on both fixtures.
why: homr passes one kernel to each, and getStructuringElement's ellipse is cell for cell cv2's.
evidence: makeLinesStronger(mask-denoised-staff.png) equals mask-filtered-staff.png with 0 pixels differing on both pages (31 230 and 63 470 pixels added). prepareBraceDotImage equals mask-brace_dot.png with 0 differing: 36 185 set pixels on the grand-staff page, none on Kesh. Fed the staff mask before makeLinesStronger it differs in 61 pixels, so the test tells the two inputs apart.
result: Applied. REQUIRED_MEMBERS gains erode, getStructuringElement, rotatedRectangleIntersection and subtract, each with a test that a build lacking it is refused by name.

decision: mergeStaffs throws DetectionError staff-without-points where two staffs share no x, mergeStaffPoints throws StaffError where Python raises ValueError, and createStaff keeps throwing StaffError on an empty grid.
why: Fork 3 names Staff([]) as a crash site, and the sketch's StaffError there would be a second failure type for it. The ValueError is not a page outcome: resampling yields integer x, so two points with one rounded key are the same x. createStaff also serves the golden decoder, where an empty grid is a malformed file.
evidence: staff-merge.json: the six merges are exact against Python's stored grid, average_unit_size, min and max; the IndexError and ValueError cases throw the two types. Its half-even case gives the same merged staff under half-up rounding, so a hand test holds Python's answers for 100.5 with 101.4 (IndexError) and 102.5 with 101.6 (ValueError).
result: Applied. A caller standing where Python builds Staff([]) checks for an empty grid itself and throws the DetectionError.

decision: constants.ts gains the 16 values detection reads and leaves four of constants.py out.
why: tolerance_for_staff_at_any_point is read only by the clef connection finder, which never has a clef to test. tolerance_note_grouping has no reader, and black_spot_removal_threshold and duration_of_quarter belong to staff parsing and the xml writer.
evidence: grep of constants.<name> over the installed package, by module.
result: Applied. Staff.symbols and StaffOptions.symbols are readonly and nothing in src wrote to them.

decision: staff-tolerance.ts holds the staff, note, notehead and multi-staff comparisons; the anchor and raw-staff ones wait for their types. compareBoxLists takes an optional pathOf.
why: StaffAnchor and RawStaff do not exist until their constructors are ported. A stem is a member of a note, so its failure line has to say notes[7].stem and not stems[5]. compareNoteheadLists returns the report without positionsExact, which a notehead does not have.
evidence: On both fixtures staffs.json, notes.json, noteheads-with-stems.json and multistaffs.json compare equal to themselves with every worst delta 0. A copy with one ordinate moved by 1e-6 fails naming staffs[1].grid[7].y[2]; a changed position, stem, direction, ellipse, grouping or count each fails naming its path. A grid shifted by 10 px is one line that counts the points, 185 on Kesh's second staff, not a line per point.
result: Applied. Both tolerances are still the starting values: fromPythonInputs (1e-9) stays reasoned, not measured, until a stage produces a staff.

decision: BOX_RECT_TOLERANCE.center moves from 3e-4 to 4e-4. Size and angle stay.
why: break_wide_fragments refits each piece with minAreaRect, and one piece of the grand-staff page is 3.66e-4 off Python's centre. The cause is traced: rotatingCalipers computes dx*a + dy*b in float32, the arm64 cv2 build contracts it into a fused multiply-add, and WebAssembly has no fused multiply-add, so opencv.js rounds twice where Python rounds once. A centre delta is therefore a whole number of float32 ulps of the coordinate. An ulp is 1.22e-4 from 1024 to 2048, and the old bound was two ulps and a margin.
evidence: Over the 899 broken fragments of the two pages the centre deltas are 0, 1, 2 or 3 ulps of the coordinate. The largest is fragment 275 of the grand-staff page, a nine-point contour at x 1776.86: 3 ulps in x, 2 in y. Contours, ids and sizes are exact on that entry. The disassembly of cv::minAreaRect in the arm64 wheel shows 16 fused multiply-adds, and a TypeScript calipers port that emulates them is bit-identical to Python on 2573 of 2573 golden rects of both pages, where opencv.js is identical on 2111, within 1e-3 on 460 and wrong on 2. docs/design/phase-5-minarearect.md.
result: Applied in src/golden/box-tolerance.ts with the cause in its comment. The bound admits three ulps on a page up to 2048 px wide and not four. Phase 4's lists pass unchanged; the two pinned noteheads still fail as pinned. The calipers are not ported and the pin stays: whether the port follows the arm64 oracle or an x86_64 server, whose wheel has no fused instruction there, is the owner's open decision.

decision: STAFF_TOLERANCES.fromPythonInputs stays 1e-9, and is now measured.
why: It was reasoned from Math.tan against libm's tan. Stage 3 is the first to produce a staff.
evidence: From Python's broken fragments, clefs and bar lines, detectStaff gives 8 of 8 staffs on the grand-staff page (173, 169, 176, 175, 182, 177, 181 and 173 points) and 4 of 4 on Kesh (190, 185, 188, 180), every x exact. Worst ordinate delta 5.7e-14 and worst unit size 1.4e-14 on the grand-staff page, every angle exact, Kesh exact throughout. The anchors' averageUnitSize, minY and maxY equal Python's stored values with delta 0 on all 293.
result: No bound moved. The comment on fromPythonInputs holds the numbers.

decision: decodeStaffAnchors and decodeRawStaffs build StaffAnchor and RawStaff through their factories. GoldenStaffAnchor and GoldenRawStaff are gone.

A RawStaff's box is still Python's stored rect and polygon, through rawStaffFromParts, because the decoder has no opencv.js; the fit itself is checked by the find_raw_staffs row, where the port's box equals Python's on all 12 staffs with delta 0.

decision: StaffLineSegment has no debugId, and four small exports join the module map: mapFiveLines, rawStaffContour, rawStaffFromParts and zoneColumns.

The four exports are what the decoder, the tuple type and the zone row need: a RawStaff around a stored box, its contour, a map that keeps five lines five, and image[:, zone].

decision: The noise filter is plain TypeScript and the grid's cast is Uint8Array's own.
why: The synthesis chose it: a 0/255 tile under an integer kernel sums exactly in any order, and each tile reflects at its own edges. A page under 20 px either way throws a PlaneError where Python divides by zero.
evidence: noise.json of both pages: 420 tile values exact on each, outcome clean, and the page object returned is the one given. vectors/noise.json: grid, filtered count, total, outcome and mask exact on its 9 cases, the 2040 stored as 248 and the short last tiles included. On the masked case all seven planes come back zeroed on the filtered tiles and untouched elsewhere.
result: Applied in src/geometry/noise-filter.ts. src/golden/page.ts imports NOISE_GRID_DIVISIONS from it.

decision: The hand tests of test/staff-chain.test.ts and one of test/raw-staffs.test.ts hold expected values printed by homr itself from a throwaway script, because the oracle has no dump for them.
why: A mutation run showed nine wrong readings of the Python that no page and no vector noticed, the non_parallel index and the direction of the left walk among them. The golden and vector files were not to be regenerated in this stage.
evidence: Missing from tools/dump-vectors.py, each now covered by a hand case with Python's answer: connect_staff_lines where a short fragment runs the clean-up; find_staff_anchors with a unit of 2.5 and a sixth line; a bar line one unit off its lines; resample_staff with a missing top line beside a too-close pair, and on a sloped staff; filter_edge_of_vision's five conditions; RawStaff.merge with two fragments at one centre x; filter_line_peaks' groups. Missing from tools/dump-golden.py: predict_other_anchors_from_clefs before its overlap filter, which is 3 boxes on the grand-staff page and 1 on Kesh, all dropped; the port builds the same rects and polygons.

decision: Fifty-two single wrong readings of the Python were applied to the port one at a time, and forty-nine fail a test.
why: Every staff row passed on its first run, so a passing row proved nothing about what it could catch.
evidence: The script is not committed. The three that survive: a left-fold mean in are_lines_parallel, which differs from numpy's only at an exact 10 degree tie and whose sum pairwise.json pins; an exclusive zone stop in find_raw_staffs, which needs a fragment centred on the last row of a zone five units below the staff; and a sample standard deviation in filter_unusual_anchors, which no two-valued set of unit sizes separates from the population one.

decision: rotatedBoxOf in src/cv/box-fitting.ts is gone and its three callers use rotatedBoxFromRect.

decision: One scope for detectStaff holds 433 Mats on Kesh and 638 on the grand-staff page.

decision: Stage 3's hand cases are vector files: connect-lines-cleanup, find-anchors, resample, edge-of-vision, raw-staff-merge and line-peak-groups join the eleven, and test/staff-chain.test.ts holds no literal.
why: The expected values were copied from a throwaway script, so nothing regenerated them and nothing recorded their oracle. A new file per rule keeps every existing vector file byte-identical.

The ten stage 3 mutations these cases were written for each fail a test that reads them, and so do two more on the other-clefs box.

decision: other-clefs.json is a new golden file per page: the boxes predict_other_anchors_from_clefs builds before it drops those overlapping a clef anchor's symbol.
why: Both pages drop every box, so staff-anchors.json holds an empty list and the box arithmetic had no oracle. A new file leaves staff-anchors.json byte-identical.
evidence: 3 boxes on the grand-staff page and 1 on Kesh, rect and polygon exact from the port. The dumper filters its own list and exits unless that equals homr's result. meta.json of both pages gains the one stage name, because the dumper lists the directory and test/golden.test.ts checks it. The other 109 files that existed before stage 4 are byte-identical by sha256, after restoring the three OpenCV 5 Kesh files the dump rewrites.
