decision: The cause of the two pinned noteheads is traced, and the port is left as it is.
why: The row of this date that pinned noteheads 18 and 48 called the cause new and unknown. It is the same as the centre tolerance's: on those two contours the upright and the rotated rectangle have exactly equal area, the fused multiply-add of the arm64 build keeps the tie and the two roundings of WebAssembly break it.
evidence: docs/design/phase-5-minarearect.md: 53 of 2573 golden contours have an exact tie, the two arithmetics choose differently on 2 of them, and opencv-python 4.12 native returns what 4.14 native returns. The x86_64 wheel of the same release has no fused instruction in minAreaRect, so homr on Linux very probably returns what opencv.js returns; that was not run.
result: Open for the owner: port the calipers to match the arm64 oracle, or move the oracle to x86_64. KNOWN_DIVERGENCES stays and minAreaRect is untouched.

decision: adjustBbox, checkBboxSize, splitClumpsOfNoteheads and addNotesToStaffs are ported, and notehead-clumps.json is a new vector file for them.
why: notehead-splits.json is empty on both pages: no notehead is split, so the pages check only that nothing splits. bbox-split.json stops at check_bbox_size and never builds a piece or a note.
evidence: From Python's staffs and noteheads: 80 of 80 notes on Kesh and 102 of 102 on the grand-staff page, every position, stem and ellipse exact, 21 18 19 22 and 16 8 15 15 12 16 13 7 notes per staff. bbox-split.json: 14 cases exact. notehead-clumps.json: 14 cases through add_notes_to_staffs with a self-check against the dumper's unrolled copy, pieces and notes exact, among them a staff that steps under a clump (the pieces are measured at the clump's x), a clump above row 0 (int() truncates the corner, and a top of -1 selects no rows), a note on two staffs, and points whose unit differs from the staff's.
result: Applied in src/geometry/notes.ts. addNotesToStaffs returns new staffs and the given ones are checked untouched.

decision: check_bbox_size's second pass is ported literally, and for a real page it changes nothing.
why: The findings and the brief both named the second pass as a trap. Worked through, a box the height split yields has round(h / unit) of 1 again unless h // n is half a unit or less, which needs a unit of about two pixels.
evidence: A port without the second pass passed every case until notehead-clumps.json gained one with a unit of 2, where Python drops all four boxes and keeps the notehead whole. The stage 1 case named for the second pass, a thin right half, loses that half in the first pass.
result: Kept literal, with the case that tells the two apart. The comment on checkBboxSize says what the pass does.

decision: The brace stage is ported in src/geometry/braces.ts, with three new vector files: braces-units, multi-staff-merge and grand-staffs.
why: braces.json in the vectors runs the whole function, where a merged entry is always the last of the list and every staff has one unit size, so the move to the end, the first-staff and closest-staff units of the tall filter and the thresholds of the score had no oracle.
evidence: Both pages: tall, connections, merged and multistaffs.json exact row by row, 21 tall of 25 boxes, 8 connected pairs and 4 grand staffs on the grand-staff page, 4 single staffs on Kesh. The 25 brace_dot boxes come out of the port's own fit with centre, size and angle deltas of 0. braces.json 13 cases, braces-units.json 5, multi-staff-merge.json 6 and grand-staffs.json 12, all exact. scoreBraceWithStaffPair equals Python's score on every pair and brace, 194 for a brace at the left edge.
result: Applied. The two connection finders that read bar lines and clefs off a staff are not ported; nothing puts either on a staff in 0.7.0. With two staffs and no brace Python's max() raises and the port scores nothing; a multi staff of two was joined by a brace, so the list is never empty.

decision: formatStaffPositions writes staff-positions.txt byte for byte from Python's multi staffs.
why: The app's server route consumes this file, and homr computes the centre as x1 + width / 2 before dividing by the image size.
evidence: Both pages: 4 lines each, identical bytes, final newline included. A hand case with lines at 0.1 and 0.7 prints 0.0004 where (y1 + y2) / 2 prints 0.00039999999999999996; the expected string is Python's own.
result: Applied in src/pipeline/staff-positions.ts.

decision: detectStaffsInImage reproduces Python from the raw masks on both pages, with the order of some notes pinned by index as a known difference.
why: combine_noteheads_with_stems sorts noteheads by centre y. Noteheads on one staff height have centres one or two float32 ulps apart, and the port's centres differ from Python's by as much, which is the fused multiply-add cause of the centre tolerance. So the sort puts such neighbours in another order. The brief expected one swap on the grand-staff page and none on Kesh; that came from a run that patched Python on two contours only and did not model the ulp noise on the others.
evidence: Kesh: 12 of 80 notes sit at another index, in five groups whose Python centres are within 6.2e-5 px of each other in y. Grand-staff page: 4 of 102, one pair from ulp noise and the pair 83 and 84 from notehead 18. Matched by contour, every note has Python's position, stem and direction, and every ellipse but the two pinned ones is within the box tolerance. Grouping 1 1 1 1 on both pages, staff ordinates within 2.5e-4 px and angles within 3.8e-6 degrees, inside fromOwnBoxes. The staff-positions text has the class, centre x and width identical and the two y columns within 2 * 3e-4 / height.
result: Applied in test/detect-golden.test.ts. REORDERED lists every moved index and REFITTED the two ellipses; the test fails if a listed entry starts to match or an unlisted one stops, and checks that each moved note took the place of one within the centre tolerance of its own height. No tolerance moved. Deviation from the brief, which asked for one named swap.

decision: The one Mat scope of detectStaffsInImage holds 1528 Mats on Kesh and 2313 on the grand-staff page.
why: The synthesis asked for the estimate of about 1500 to be measured when detect.ts ran.
evidence: Counted by a spy on MatScope.keep under Node. The whole call takes 620 ms on Kesh and 760 ms on the grand-staff page. The grand-staff page is over the estimate because each connection test thickens the brace and builds two staff-point boxes, 21 tall boxes times 14 ordered staff pairs.
result: Recorded. Not reduced: the Mats are four-point outlines and are freed when the call returns.

decision: 76 single wrong readings of the Python were applied to notes, braces, staff positions and detect one at a time, and 71 fail a test.
why: Every row of stage 4 passed on its first run. The first round caught 58 of 76, and the 18 survivors named the cases that braces-units.json, the mixed-unit case of grand-staffs.json, four cases of notehead-clumps.json and two hand tests were then written for.
evidence: The five that survive are equivalent on any reachable input: an offset that differs only for a box that starts above row 0 and ends below the mask; a second pass that only splits by height; the first size gate, which the piece gate repeats; a score at overlap equal to distance, which is 0 either way; and a connected staff also listed alone, which the merge absorbs.
result: Recorded. The script is not committed.

decision: The bench page runs detection after segmentation and draws the staffs over the preprocessed page, and it was run in Chrome on both fixtures.
why: This is the phase's runtime check: the chain on the library's own masks, in the browser, with nothing golden in it.
evidence: Chrome on WebGPU, apple metal-3, cross-origin isolated. Kesh: 4 multi staffs, 80 notes, detection 1139, 1103 and 1098 ms over three runs. Grand-staff page: 4 grand staffs, 21 connections, 102 notes, 1166, 1143 and 1124 ms. On both overlays the lines drawn from staff.grid sit on the printed lines, with the excursions of 3 to 5 px under beams that Python's own staffs.json has, and the four braces are outlined and bracketed. Segmentation took 700 to 800 ms per page in the same runs.
result: Applied in bench/bench.js and bench/index.html, with rgbaFromPlane in src/image/plane.ts as the one library addition. The page takes ?fixture= for the second page.

decision: Do not port the fused multiply-add calipers; the port keeps opencv.js's minAreaRect and the pinned divergences stay.
why: The owner states the port will run on arm64 and x86_64 machines alike. WebAssembly has no fused multiply-add on any of them, so opencv.js gives one answer everywhere, while native homr gives the arm64 answer on an Apple Silicon Mac and very probably the opencv.js answer on x86_64. Emulating the arm64 build would make every browser reproduce one native build's tie-break and move the port away from the other.
evidence: docs/design/phase-5-minarearect.md: 53 of 2573 golden contours have an exact minimum-area tie and the two arithmetics disagree on 2; matched by contour, every note position, stem and direction equals Python's. The x86_64 wheel was disassembled, not run.
result: Not applied. KNOWN_DIVERGENCES in test/boxes-golden.test.ts and REORDERED and REFITTED in test/detect-golden.test.ts stay. Open: regenerate the goldens on x86_64 if the Linux server is x86_64, which would remove the pins.

decision: Kesh canvas-1.png, tokens-1.json and voices.json are re-dumped under the pinned OpenCV 4.14.0.
why: The three files dated from phase 0 (972696a), when the oracle ran OpenCV 5 unnoticed. Phase 5 re-ran the dumper under 4.14 but the commit of that run did not carry them, so meta.json said 4.14 over a canvas made by 5.
evidence: npm run golden changes exactly these three files and nothing else. The old and new canvas-1 differ on 1397 of 327680 pixels, mean absolute difference 0.0052; 48 coordinate values of tokens-1 move, by at most 1.07 pixels, and no other field of the 24 tokens changes. The other seven canvases are byte-identical.
result: Committed as the oracle for phase 6.

decision: dump-golden.py unrolls prepare_staff_image and writes dewarp-<n>.json with three images per canvas: the first crop, the warped crop and the cleaned second crop.
why: Each stage test reads the Python output of the stage before. Without the intermediates the warp test would start from the TypeScript resize and crop, and a resize difference would read as a triangulation difference.
evidence: The script exits unless the unrolled canvas equals prepare_staff_image byte for byte and the staffs serialise identically; it passed on both pages. Every existing golden file is byte-identical except meta.json, which lists the 16 new files per page. 6 of 8 canvases have an identity transform (every matrix the identity); Kesh canvas 1 shifts all 169 triangles by up to 1 px, grand-staff canvas 3 shifts 30 of 122 by up to 2 px.
result: Applied; findings in docs/design/phase-6-findings.md.

decision: Three vector files: staff-regrouping (the four branches of _ensure_same_number_of_staffs, StaffRegions, get_tr_omr_canvas_size), dewarp-points (span and optimal points and the transform on hand staffs) and dewarp-warp (two synthetic curved staffs, 4 and 12 px, warped by homr, with find_simplex and transform_point probes).
why: Both pages take the first regrouping branch and are near identity, so the other branches, the zero-reference truthiness test and a real warp had no oracle. No photograph is on this machine; dewarp-warp is the only non-trivial warp the suite can check.
evidence: Every existing vector file is byte-identical. 7 + 1, 8 and 2 cases.
result: Applied.

decision: The triangulation is delaunator over the points plus the three outer vertices Subdiv2D::initDelaunay adds, with every triangle touching one dropped; Subdiv2D's insertion order is not ported.
why: Subdiv2D triangulates the points together with three virtual vertices 6 * max(w, h) from the rect (read back with getVertex on the oracle), so flat triangles along the image edge, whose circumcircle holds a virtual vertex, are missing from homr's mesh and warp_image leaves those pixels at fill 1. Plain delaunator covers the whole hull.
evidence: Plain delaunator: Kesh 172 triangles where homr has 169, 93 of them common, and the warp off on 31412 to 33613 pixels per canvas, mean 22.1 to 24.2. Augmented delaunator: the triangle count equals homr's on all 8 canvases, 116 of 122 and 163 of 169 triangles common (3 co-circular cells take the other diagonal), and the warp from homr's own input and control points is exact on 7 of 8 canvases; grand-staff canvas 3 differs on 3 pixels, mean 0.00006. dewarp-warp.json, two curved staffs: 47 pixels (mean 0.0076) at 4 px of curve and 30 (mean 0.0091) at 12 px. The warp on homr's own mesh is exact on all 8 canvases and both curves.
result: Applied in src/dewarp/delaunay.ts. The ceiling of 1.0 holds with three orders of magnitude to spare, so the port of Subdiv2D is not needed.

decision: getAffineTransform's matrices are compared to 1e-9, not exactly.
why: opencv.js solves the 6 by 6 system in WebAssembly and native cv2 with SIMD; the matrices differ in the last bits.
evidence: Largest difference over all 8 canvases 1.4e-11. The warp on those matrices is still exact on every canvas.
result: Applied in test/dewarp-golden.test.ts.

decision: Every cv2.resize of this phase is compared to within two gray levels.
why: The oracle's cv2 is the arm64 wheel, built with the KleidiCV 26.03 and Carotene HAL (getBuildInformation), and its INTER_LINEAR is not OpenCV's generic fixed point. Against the exact bilinear value on Kesh canvas 0's centring, native is off by up to 1.93 levels and opencv.js by up to 0.53, so the two differ by up to 2. setUseOptimized(False) does not switch the HAL off. Same class as phase 5's fused multiply-add: an arm64 native build, not a port defect.
evidence: First crop after the page resize, pixels differing: Kesh 4886, 4847, 3328, 4587; grand-staff 7239, 8389, 6104, 5069; never more than 1 level. Centring: Kesh 3335, 2770, 2552, 2831 at up to 2 levels; grand-staff 11, 0, 0, 5.
result: Applied in test/staff-image.test.ts as RESIZE_TOLERANCE. Not emulated.

decision: staffCanvases reproduces homr's canvases from multistaffs.json and preprocessed.png within the typeset ceiling on both pages.
why: The end-to-end check of the phase, the stage tests having each started from Python's own input.
evidence: Mean absolute difference per canvas, grand-staff 0 to 3: 0.0161, 0.0142, 0.0090, 0.0125 (5275, 4660, 2954, 4099 pixels differ); Kesh 0 to 3: 0.0220, 0.0191, 0.0143, 0.0203 (6795, 6017, 4461, 6332). Ceiling 1.0. The returned staff matches canvas-<n>-staff.json within 1e-9. Region, canvas size, scale, crop corners, control points, the second crop and the clean-up are exact.
result: Applied.

decision: StaffCanvas keeps phase 1's two fields, image and staff; the phase file's scaling and topLeft are not added, and the staff is documented as homr returns it.
why: prepare_staff_image returns the staff moved and scaled into the first crop, not dewarped and not in the canvas, and nothing reads a scaling or a top-left after it.
evidence: canvas-<n>-staff.json equals staffInCrop of the multi staff's staff on all 8 canvases.
result: Applied. Whether phase 7 needs the staff in true canvas coordinates is phase 7's question; homr does not have it either.

decision: The phase file's module names become src/dewarp/piecewise-affine.ts and src/pipeline/staff-image.ts, and the regrouping is _ensure_same_number_of_staffs.
why: Phases 4 and 5 name modules in kebab case. 0.7.0 has no _find_periodic_core; the phase file names a function of a later homr.
evidence: grep over the installed homr finds no periodic function.
result: Applied.

decision: 45 single wrong readings of the Python were applied to the dewarp, the control points and staff-image.ts one at a time, and 37 fail a test.
why: Every stage test passed on its first run against the pages, which are flat and never exercise the clean-up, so a first round caught 29 of 45. Its survivors named three new vector inputs: black-contours.json (nine images through remove_black_contours_at_edges_of_image), five more dewarp-points cases (three and two points on a row, a point on each margin, a steep rise) with homr's matrices now compared, and two regrouping cases with _calculate_region per staff (an odd system of two, a staff past the left edge).
evidence: The 8 survivors: rounding instead of truncating the fillConvexPoly vertices, not cloning the roi, >= at the canvas aspect ratio, and the mean of the mapped x are equivalent on every input 0.7.0 can produce (the control points are integers, warpAffine with BORDER_CONSTANT reads nothing outside the roi, both branches give 1280 by 256 at equality, staffInCrop maps x independently of y); the roi clone was then removed as dead weight. Moving the virtual vertices 10 px at a distance of about 8000 changes neither the triangle count nor how many triangles match homr on any of the 8 canvases. Python round half up on the scaled region has no .5 product on either page. Skipping the clean-up in prepareStaffImage is invisible on both pages, which never clean anything; the stage itself is checked by black-contours.json. Voice-major canvas order has no oracle: no public page has two voices.
result: Applied; the survivors are recorded here rather than tested.

decision: The bench runs staffCanvases on the last run's own detection and shows each canvas above homr's canvas-<n>.png with their mean absolute difference and both regions; it was run in Chrome on both fixtures. The import map gains delaunator and robust-predicates.
why: This is the phase's runtime check: the whole chain in the browser on the browser's own masks.
evidence: Chrome, apple metal-3, cross-origin isolated. staffCanvases takes 140 ms on Kesh and 111 ms on the grand-staff page. Grand-staff on WebGPU: 0.0161, 0.0142, 0.0090, 0.0125, every region homr's. Kesh on fp32 wasm: 0.0220, 0.0191, 0.0143, 0.0203, the Node numbers exactly. Kesh on WebGPU: canvas 2 is 8.1966 and the other three are the Node numbers. Its region is 82,797,1817,1025 where homr's is 82,797,1817,1026: the fp16 staff mask has 135171 pixels where fp32 has 135163, the staff's max_y + 4 units falls the other side of an integer, the crop loses a row and the scale changes. From homr's own multistaffs.json the same browser gives 0.0143.
result: Recorded, not fixed. A one-pixel region change is phase 6 faithfully following a staff that fp16 moved; whether it changes a token is phase 7's to measure on the WebGPU path.

decision: Design: TokenSequence is readonly DecodedSymbol[]; DecoderState is a class that borrows the decoder ModelSession and owns every tensor of one decode; runDecoder checks an AbortSignal before each step.
why: ModelStore owns sessions and shares them across staffs, so a decode that closed its session would close it for the next staff. What a cancelled decode must give back is its 32 caches. The feeds are one object whose five int64 id tensors and cache_len wrap typed arrays overwritten in place, because onnxruntime copies inputs into its heap when a run starts (the segnet buffer relies on the same). context[:, :1] is built once, after step 0.
evidence: test/decoder-loop.test.ts drives a scripted session: BOS and nonote at step 0, each argmax fed back, cache_len 0, 1, 2, the context rows 1280 then 1, cache_out<i> fed back as cache_in<i>, every cache disposed on EOS, on the 608-step limit and on an abort, which rejects with the signal's reason after exactly the steps already run.
result: Applied in src/transformer/decoder.ts. Phase 9's Worker passes its own signal; architect skipped, a literal port with the one performance choice prescribed by the spec.

decision: The phase file's modules become src/transformer/normalize.ts, encoder.ts, decoder.ts, duration.ts, remove-duplicated-symbols.ts and src/pipeline/parse-staffs.ts; remove_tuplet and to_upper_position join symbol.ts; the position filter is filterPositions in parse-staffs.ts.
why: vocabulary.ts is generated tables imported by symbol.ts, so remove_duplicated_symbols there would make an import cycle. Kebab case as in phases 4 to 6. The position filter is one line of staff_parsing_tromr.py and sits with its only caller.
evidence: grep of the installed homr.
result: Applied.

decision: Only the part of vocabulary.py that parse_staffs reaches is ported: remove_duplicated_symbols, its six helpers, kern durations, remove_tuplet, to_upper_position. change_lift, add_* and strip_* articulations and slurs, sort_token_chords, is_valid and __lt__ wait for phase 9.
why: Their callers are circle_of_fifths.py and music_xml_generator.py, which are phase 9. Porting them now gives them no oracle and no caller.
evidence: grep over the installed homr: change_lift in circle_of_fifths.py, sort_token_chords and get_duration in music_xml_generator.py, nothing on the parse_staffs path.
result: Plan change: phase 9 ports them with the writer.

decision: Two homr bugs in vocabulary.py are ported as they are: a longer duplicate pitch is stored under the pitch alone and never replaces the first, and the multirest branch of kern_to_symbol_duration returns nothing, so rest_2m reads as a half.
why: The oracle has them and voices.json depends on them.
evidence: vocabulary-cleanup.json: "chord with a longer duplicate pitch" keeps note_8 where note_4 would win, and get_duration of rest_2m is 1/2.
result: Applied.

decision: Two vector files: vocabulary-cleanup (17 symbol lists through remove_duplicated_symbols with and without cleanup_tuplets, 14 remove_tuplet rhythms, 18 durations, 10 prior_power_of_two) and normalize (ConvertToArray on all 256 gray values, as float32 and as the float16 bits encoder_inference.py casts to). dump-golden.py is unchanged.
why: Both pages are plain tunes: no chords to deduplicate, no tuplets to remove, no lower clef. The tokens matched on the first run, so no transformer intermediate was needed.
evidence: tools/dump-vectors.py vocabulary-cleanup normalize; every existing vector file keeps its sha256.
result: Applied.

decision: Tokens are equal on every staff of both fixtures, encoder and decoder fp32 on WebAssembly under Node, from Python's canvases.
why: The phase's target: a token difference is a port bug until a logit measurement says otherwise.
evidence: test/transformer-golden.test.ts: grand-staff canvases 0 to 3 give 41, 53, 48, 35 tokens, Kesh 29, 24, 26, 28, each equal to tokens-<n>.json on all six heads. parseStaffs from multistaffs.json and preprocessed.png, through the port's own canvases, gives voices.json's heads exactly on both pages.
result: Exact. No tolerance on tokens.

decision: The attention coordinates are compared within 6 px, not exactly.
why: They are a float32 output of the same graph and move by whole pixels under changes that leave every token alone: native onnxruntime 1.x on the oracle with ORT_DISABLE_ALL and one intra-op thread moves them against its own default run by 3.34 px on Kesh canvas 2, 5.13 on grand-staff canvas 2 and 2.49 on Kesh canvas 3, tokens identical. homr's own comment calls them imprecise attention, not localisation.
evidence: The port against tokens-<n>.json, worst per canvas: grand-staff 1.895, 3.974, 4.756, 1.945; Kesh 0.899, 0.841, 3.084, 0.001 px. The probe re-ran Staff2Score and a second session pair on canvas-<n>.png in the oracle's venv; the default run reproduced the golden coordinates exactly.
result: Applied in test/transformer-golden.test.ts. The ceiling is the measured native self-variation, rounded up.

decision: 47 single wrong readings of the Python were applied to durations, remove_duplicated_symbols, symbol.ts, normalize, the decoder loop and parse-staffs one at a time, and 44 fail a test.
why: Every token matched on the first run, and both pages are plain tunes, so the first round let ten through: the shortest note of a chord, a grace note in a chord, the median of an even measure count, the half table, the 608 limit, an empty staff, among them.
evidence: First round 37 of 47. Its survivors named vocabulary-cleanup.json's new measure and typical cases (Python's _get_duration_of_measure and _get_typical_duration_of_measures), an encoderInput test over every gray value in both element types, 608 as a literal and an empty staff in the voice join. The three left are equivalent on any reachable input: the default base 4 of a kern with no digits (every rhythm token has digits), swapping the tuplet and lower-clef steps (one reads durations only and writes rhythms, the other reads clefs and writes positions), and startsWith("key") for "keySignature" (no other rhythm starts with key).
result: Applied in commit 76e362d. One golden run in the second round failed with no mutation that could change a token (the default base) and passed when rerun alone; the cause was not identified.

decision: Timings: about 18 ms a decoder step under Node WebAssembly on one thread, 28 to 36 ms in Chrome on four threads; the encoder about 1.85 s per staff on WebAssembly and 250 to 300 ms fp16 on WebGPU.
why: The plan's baseline is 28 to 45 ms a step on WebAssembly, which this phase must not regress.
evidence: Node (startRuntime maxBackend wasm, one thread): 17.7 to 19.7 ms a step, encoder and step 0 1.85 to 1.92 s, 2.3 to 2.8 s a staff. Chrome, apple metal-3, cross-origin isolated, four threads: on WebGPU 28.3 to 33.3 ms a step and 0.93 to 1.96 s a staff (the first encoder run 651 ms, then 242 to 308 ms); on wasm-threads 31.2 to 40.6 ms a step and 2.6 to 3.5 s a staff, the encoder 1.7 to 2.1 s. Steps 25 to 54 per staff.
result: Recorded; within the baseline. One thread in Node beats four in Chrome per step, unexplained: phase 9 should measure the decoder at numThreads 1 in the browser before choosing.

decision: On WebGPU (fp16 encoder) every token of both pages equals tokens-<n>.json, on homr's canvases and on the port's own; Kesh canvas 2, one pixel row off on WebGPU, changes no token. No fp16 argmax flip was seen.
why: Phase 6 left the question of the shifted canvas to this phase, and the fp16 encoder could flip a rare argmax.
evidence: The bench runs parseStaffCanvas twice per canvas and compares the six heads. Kesh on WebGPU: canvas 2's region ends at 1025 where homr's ends at 1026, mean absolute difference 8.1966, and its 26 tokens are homr's. All 8 canvases equal on webgpu and on wasm-threads, from both canvases.
result: Recorded. The fp16 path is proven on these two typeset pages only.

decision: tools/export-decoder.py runs homr's convert_decoder at v0.7.0 (8b5dcf7) on the checkpoints release's pytorch_model_396 in .venv-export (torch 2.7.1, x-transformers 2.16.1, homr's poetry.lock pins), and skips simplify.py, fuse.py and quantization.py. convert_encoder is not run.
why: The shipped decoder is fused (SkipLayerNormalization, com.microsoft) and int8; the shipped fp16 encoder already runs on the WebGPU EP. A separate venv leaves the oracle's packages alone.
evidence: Two runs give the same fp32 file, SHA-256 16ab65f1fdf6c119eeb921ede4e76d7f0f0d545da86b51a9874311c4ae41443d, 187,986,952 bytes: the int8 file is 47 MB, so fp32 is about 188 MB, not the 85 MB the phase file estimated. Opset 18, no com.microsoft domain, one If node.
result: Applied. The fp32 file stays local; only the fp16 one is in the manifest.

decision: The fp16 decoder keeps float32 inputs and outputs (keep_io_types), and export-decoder.py repairs two things onnxconverter-common 1.16 leaves float32 inside the graph.
why: float32 at the edges is the phase 7 contract, so DecoderState does not change. As converted the model does not load: each cache_out<i> is cast back to float32 at the edge while its own layer's Einsum still reads the float32 name, and x-transformers' Cast(to=float) after the attention softmax is not rewritten.
evidence: Readers of an edge cast are pointed at the half it consumes, internal Casts to float become Casts to half, value_info is dropped; onnx.checker passes and onnxruntime 1.24.1 and onnxruntime-web 1.30.0 both load it. SHA-256 253172b02c50883e3f41beb6e842cf707596de8b2f7497a52ed7a01b3f76a27a, 94,133,299 bytes. gen-manifest refuses a decoder whose input or output names and types differ from decoder-396-fp32's.
result: Applied.

decision: tools/verify-decoder.py: both re-exports give the shipped decoder's tokens on every staff, through homr's own ScoreDecoder on the CPU EP, the shipped fp32 encoder feeding all three.
why: The phase's Python gate; the decoders are the only variable.
evidence: All six heads equal: grand-staff 41, 53, 48, 35 tokens and Kesh 29, 24, 26, 28, fp32 and fp16 alike. The attention coordinates move against the int8 decoder's by up to 8.95 px fp32 and 8.79 px fp16 (Kesh canvas 1) with every token equal.
result: Exact on tokens. The 6 px coordinate tolerance of test/transformer-golden.test.ts is not applied to the re-export; its golden test compares tokens only.

decision: On the WebGPU EP (Chrome, apple metal-3, cross-origin isolated) the fp16 re-export with the fp16 encoder gives tokens-<n>.json on all 8 staffs, on homr's canvases and on the port's own. The If node and the zero-sized step-0 caches need no change.
why: The two risks the phase file named, and the fp16 argmax question.
evidence: bench ?decoder=webgpu, both fixtures: every line "equal to tokens-<n>.json". Step 0 feeds 32 zero-length CPU tensors; from step 1 the caches are GPU buffers (WEBGPU_DECODER_CATALOG keeps every cache_out on the GPU), and onnxruntime-web 1.30.0 takes the mix. Kesh canvas 2, a pixel row off on WebGPU, still gives homr's 26 tokens. No fp16 argmax flip seen. Under Node the same artifacts on the wasm EP give every token too (golden test, 16 staffs).
result: No fixed-branch export needed.

decision: The default decoder placement stays on WebAssembly on a WebGPU runtime; WEBGPU_DECODER_CATALOG is the opt-in.
why: One token per run is a few hundred tiny kernels and is dispatch-bound on the GPU.
evidence: Chrome, apple metal-3, same session: WebGPU decoder 78.4 to 79.7 ms a step on grand-staff and 77.0 to 84.7 on Kesh (one outlier 153.2) with the caches on the GPU, 129.3 to 135.9 ms on Kesh with them read back each step; the shipped decoder on four wasm threads 21.7 to 22.7 ms a step on grand-staff. Phase 7: Node one thread 17.7 to 19.7, Chrome wasm-threads 31.2 to 40.6.
result: Plan change: the WebGPU decoder is correct and 3 to 4 times slower. Encoder on WebGPU, decoder on wasm threads remains the fastest arrangement measured.

decision: The MusicXML writer is generate_xml with default XmlGeneratorArguments, written through a small XmlElement that orders note, pitch, attributes and barline children by the schema; relieur.py and circle_of_fifths.py are not ported.
why: The server runs homr with no large page, metronome or tempo. homr's musicxml package places children in XSD sequence order. relieur.py does not exist in 0.7.0 and nothing imports circle_of_fifths.py.
evidence: test/musicxml.test.ts: 32 vectors (dump-vectors.py musicxml) canonically equal with equal log lines; voices.json of both pages gives page.musicxml byte for byte. 7 of 8 single wrong readings fail; the (start, end) sort key survives because ends never tie out of order within a measure.
result: Applied.

decision: staves.json is written by the app server's own parseOmrStaves through tools/dump-staves.sh, and staffBoxes is computed from the numbers formatStaffPositions prints, with no string round trip.
why: Python prints shortest round-trip floats and Go parses them exactly, so the numbers are the server's.
evidence: test/staff-positions.test.ts: exact equality on both pages from Python's multistaffs.
result: Applied.

decision: The public API follows docs/design/phase-9-synthesis.md: an async createRecognizer that rejects when the Worker cannot start, results in the server's shape plus backend, busy instead of a queue, ids on the Worker's port, lazy models with a models progress stage, homr-web/internal for every module, SegmentationWorker deleted.
why: Two architect candidates (opus, sonnet) compared on the brief; the decisions table in the synthesis says which came from which.
evidence: test/worker.test.ts drives the client and WorkerHost together over structuredClone with a scripted engine: 9 cases. test/recognize-golden.test.ts: both pages from their PNG on Node WebAssembly give homr's MusicXML (canonical) and the server's staves within 1e-6, about 40 s a page.
result: Applied.

decision: The bench consumes createRecognizer from dist/index.js; serve.mjs rewrites bare specifiers in dist/ and delaunator, and the opencv.js shim runs the UMD through an indirect eval.
why: A module Worker in Chrome gets no import map and no working importScripts.
evidence: Chrome, apple metal-3, isolated, WebGPU: Kesh 5.06 s, page.musicxml byte-equal, staves within 1.9e-4 (the fp16 staff mask moves a staff, as phase 6 saw); grand staff 6.21 s, byte-equal, staves within 4.1e-6.
result: Applied.

decision: The wasm thread count stays at 4.
why: Phase 8 asked for the browser decoder at one thread before a default is picked.
evidence: Chrome, WebGPU session, decoder on wasm, Kesh, 8 staffs per run: 1 thread 42.0 to 44.0 ms a step; 4 threads 23.2 to 26.5; 8 threads 25.6 to 32.0 (hardwareConcurrency 10).
result: Kept DEFAULT_MAX_THREADS = 4.

decision: A Vite consumer needs optimizeDeps.include of 'homr-web > @techstark/opencv-js'; nothing else.
why: opencv.js is a UMD bundle; Vite's dev server does not pre-bundle dependencies reached only from a Worker, and run as an ES module the UMD throws on root.cv.
evidence: Fresh npm create vite (vanilla-ts, Vite 8.3) with the packed tarball: dev without the include fails 'Cannot set properties of undefined (setting cv)'; with it, dev and build plus preview transcribe the Kesh page, MusicXML byte-equal. wasmPaths was not needed under Vite.
result: README documents it.

decision: The build emits no source maps.
why: dist/ ships without src/, and Vite printed 'points to missing source files' for every module.
evidence: Vite dev log of the consumer project.
result: tsconfig.build.json sourceMap false.

decision: texts.json is written by the app server's own code: tools/dump-texts.sh runs parseOmrStaves and runOmrChordOcr from AbcGoDb's abcsql/omr.go in a throwaway Go test, which runs the embedded omr_chord_ocr.py with the server homr virtualenv's python on the fixture and its staff-positions.txt, then remaps the line numbers to sorted staves and stable-sorts by staff and x0. tools/dump-ocr.py writes ocr.json, every RapidOCR stage per strip, from the oracle .venv.
why: The route's texts are what the app reads, and the remap and sort happen in Go, not in the script. The per-stage file is the oracle for each port stage, as dump-golden.py is for homr.
evidence: dump-texts.sh: Kesh 2 texts, grand staff 3, chord page 19. dump-ocr.py unrolls RapidOCR.__call__ and exits non-zero unless the unrolled result equals engine(strip); it passes on the three pages.
result: Applied.

decision: Third public fixture test/fixtures/chord-study-300dpi.png: sixteen bars with chord symbols, typeset by abcjs 6.6.4 with the app's own header directives (Cinzel title, Satisfy chord symbols) through tools/typeset-fixture.html and headless Chrome.
why: The Kesh page has no chord symbol (its strips read the tempo and the word jig) and the grand-staff page only its title, so neither tests a chord. Public-repo rule: only pages the app typesets.
evidence: Oracle on it: 19 texts over 4 strips, among them two misreads ("w3" 0.618 and "L4" 0.599 where the page has Em and A7) and the F#m read as "7#m"; Em is missing on strips 0 and 3. homr reads its title as CHORD STUDY (Cinzel small caps).
result: Kept. Its golden directory is 4.6 MB.

decision: The oracle depends on the OpenCV build, by up to 0.002 in score and not at all in text or box.
why: The local server virtualenv loads opencv-python 5.0.0 (both opencv-python 5.0.0.93 and opencv-python-headless 4.14 are installed; production pins headless < 5), the repository's .venv loads 4.14.0.
evidence: omr_chord_ocr.py run with both interpreters on the three pages: 24 texts, every text and every box equal, scores differ on three texts by 0.001 to 0.002 (Kesh 0.96 against 0.959, grand staff 0.891 against 0.893, chord page 0.618 against 0.616).
result: Recorded; this is the floor under any score tolerance.

decision: detect-golden pins one grid point on the chord page: from the port's own staff fragments, multistaffs[1].staffs[0] repeats x 1770 at index 176, and the rest of that staff, its median unit size recomputed without the point, is exact.
why: From Python's fragments detect_staff is exact on the page (staffs-golden), and the port's fragment polygons are 302 exact and 5 within 1 px of Python's, the class phase-5-minarearect.md describes.
evidence: Without the point: 177 of 177 points and averageUnitSize exact; with it 178 points and averageUnitSize 17.87548 against 17.87286. Six reordered note pairs at equal heights, as the other two pages have.
result: Pinned in REGRIDDED; the test fails if the point disappears.

decision: title.json is homr's _detect_title_task unrolled in dump-golden.py: the crop rectangle, RapidOCR's raw boxes, texts and scores, and the title, checked against the real function run on a Debug rooted in a temporary directory. page.musicxml now carries the title.
why: homr's CLI, which the server runs, writes the detected title into work-title; the golden had passed "" since phase 9.
evidence: The server virtualenv's homr CLI on the three pages: The Kesh, Grand Staff Study, CHORD STUDY, equal to title.json. Every other golden file regenerated byte-identical.
result: Applied; page.musicxml differs from the old golden only in work-title.

decision: A direct port of RapidOCR 3.9.2's pipeline, not @gutenye/ocr-browser.
why: The criterion is the server's texts per strip. ocr-browser 1.4.9 is a different pipeline on the same model family: detection threshold 0.03 against RapidOCR's 0.3, no box_thresh scoring, unclip 1.5 against 1.6, sides rounded up to 32 with no 736 short-side limit, no max-side 2000, no vertical padding, no direction classifier, one recognition run per line at its own width, and its own bundled PP-OCRv4 models.
evidence: Measured on the 12 oracle strips of the three pages (24 texts) with @gutenye/ocr-node 1.4.9, the same ocr-common code, under Node: with homr-web's PP-OCRv6 det/rec and the v6 dictionary, 2 of 12 strips equal and 1 of 24 texts found; with its default v4 models, 3 of 12 and 1 of 24. It merges each row of chords into one box ("G Em Am7 D7", "C Bm Am D G"), so no chord gets an x. Bundle: ocr-browser 60 kB, ocr-common 252 kB, js-clipper 408 kB, ocr-models 15 MB unless overridden; its opencv-js 4.9 would be a second OpenCV beside the port's 4.12 (it also failed to load under Node 23 until overridden to 4.12). MIT.
result: Direct port in src/ocr/, on the port's own opencv.js and onnxruntime-web sessions.

decision: The recognition alphabet is read from the model's own bytes: models/onnx-metadata.ts walks ModelProto's top level for metadata_props, and every ModelSession carries the map.
why: RapidOCR reads the PP-OCRv6 character list from onnxruntime's custom_metadata_map; onnxruntime-web 1.30.0 exposes no custom metadata. Shipping the 18,708 characters as a generated table would put about 70 kB in every bundle, OCR or not, and could drift from the model the store verified.
evidence: ctcCharacters reproduces get_character: str.splitlines (Python's eleven line boundaries), " " appended, "blank" first: 18,710 classes, the recogniser's output width in the manifest.
result: Applied.

decision: unclip is Clipper 6.4.2's ClipperOffset for one closed polygon with round joins, ported without the closing union; the expanded rectangle comes from opencv.js minAreaRect with the corners drawn in opencv-python 4.14's angle convention by the existing float32 boxPoints.
why: The union only removes self-intersections, duplicates and collinear points, none of which changes the convex hull of an outward-grown rectangle, and minAreaRect reads only the hull. pyclipper truncates float corners to integers (measured: float input equals np.trunc input, not np.round).
evidence: test/golden/vectors/ocr-unclip.json, 240 rectangles from 3 to 1,300 px, upright, steep and turned: shapely's distance exact on 240, every pyclipper vertex present in the port's polygon on 240, the expanded rectangle exact on 59 and within 4.9e-4 on the rest (phase 5's minAreaRect drift, under its 1e-3 bound).
result: Applied.

decision: The port equals the server on all 24 texts of the three pages: same texts, same staves, same boxes; scores within 0.006, the test tolerance 0.01.
why: Text equality per strip and a box tolerance were the plan's criteria; the score is the one number that moves.
evidence: test/ocr-golden.test.ts on Node wasm: every strip's preprocess size, ratios and padding exact, every detection box exact, every classifier label and recognised text exact, recognition scores within 0.0037 of ocr.json (opencv 4.14). Against texts.json (the server venv, opencv 5.0): boxes 0 drift on 24 of 24, scores 0.001 to 0.006 on 8, the largest on "w3" (0.612 against 0.618, 0.616 under opencv 4.14). At the app's 0.6 filter every text keeps the server's side: Jtg 0.593 (0.595), L4 0.598 (0.599) below, w3 above.
result: Tolerances: score 0.01, box 5e-4 page units (one pixel is 2.8e-4 to 4.0e-4), with 0 measured.

decision: texts are returned as the server's route returns them, and the threshold is an option: minTextScore, RapidOCR's text_score, default 0.5.
why: The route's texts carry no filter beyond RapidOCR's own 0.5 (omr.go remaps and sorts only); the 0.6 MIN_OCR_SCORE is the app's, in analyzer.ts, applied to server and browser texts alike. A library default of 0.6 would make the browser result differ from the server's for the same page.
evidence: Server: omr_chord_ocr.py calls RapidOCR() with the default config, text_score 0.5; runOmrChordOcr filters nothing. App: src/utils/converters/pdfToAbc/analyzer.ts:25 MIN_OCR_SCORE = 0.6, line 198 filters input.texts.
result: Default output equals the route's; the app keeps its filter or passes minTextScore 0.6.

decision: README's Bundlers section: a Vite consumer excludes homr-web and onnxruntime-web from optimizeDeps and includes 'homr-web > @techstark/opencv-js'. This corrects phase 9's row, which tested a fresh vanilla Vite project only.
why: Measured by the lead in the AbcMusicStudio app (SvelteKit, Vite dev) with homr-web 0.1.0 from npm.
evidence: With only the include, Vite pre-bundles homr-web and rewrites new URL("./worker.js", import.meta.url) to /node_modules/.vite/deps/worker.js?worker_file&type=module, which answers 404, so createRecognizer rejects with "homr-web's worker did not load"; onnxruntime-web pre-bundled looks for its .wasm under .vite/deps (303). With the exclude added, dev works; production builds worked either way.
result: README updated; the SvelteKit caveat removed.

decision: ProgressStage gains "ocr", between "staff" and "xml", and the version goes to 0.2.0.
why: Adding a value to the union is a compile break for a consumer with an exhaustive Record over it, and the AbcMusicStudio app has one: Record<ReadingStep, string> keyed on Exclude<ProgressStage, "models">. Folding OCR into "staff" or "xml" would avoid the break and leave a bar stalled on the wrong label for the OCR's seconds.
evidence: App (main): src/utils/converters/pdfToAbc/transcribe.ts:27 ReadingStep = Exclude<ProgressStage, "models">, src/components/AbcScoreTranscribeButton.svelte:66 STEP_KEYS: Record<ReadingStep, string>. Port: the ocr stage counts strips and the title band; recognize-golden asserts the stage set.
result: Breaking for that Record; the app adds one "ocr" label.

decision: readTextStrips is a Recognizer method, not a free export of index.ts; the Worker protocol's recognize command carries a task, page (with ocr and minTextScore) or texts (with staves).
why: Reading strips needs the Worker's OpenCV and model store; a free function would need a Worker of its own. As a method it shares the one-page rule, cancellation and progress, and answers the one result shape with musicXml "" and the staves given.
evidence: test/worker.test.ts: the default page task, ocr false with minTextScore 0.6, a texts task through the busy rule, a malformed task refused.
result: Applied; readStripTexts and RapidOcr are in homr-web/internal for Node.

decision: Every OCR model run is followed by a setTimeout(0) turn of the event loop.
why: onnxruntime-web's wasm runs settle as microtasks, so the OCR's runs (detection, classifier and recogniser batches per strip, plus the title) chain without a macrotask for the whole page. A Worker could not receive a cancel in that time, and vitest's worker RPC timed out.
evidence: Before: test/ocr-golden.test.ts alone, and the full suite twice, ended with 'Timeout calling "onTaskUpdate"' (60 s) though every test passed. After: ocr-golden alone has none, same results and timings (8.8 to 10.2 s a page).
result: Applied in rapid-ocr.ts's runSingle. The rest of the pipeline was not changed; it has not shown the symptom.

decision: The three OCR models run on the WebGPU EP on a WebGPU runtime, fp32; wasm elsewhere.
why: The manifest left PP-OCR on WebGPU unmeasured for this phase to decide.
evidence: Bench, Chrome, apple metal-3, cross-origin isolated, the public API in its Worker, each placement in a fresh tab, warm run: ocr stage on WebGPU 3.30 s chord page, 3.12 s Kesh, 3.17 s grand staff; on four wasm threads 5.29, 4.71, 4.70 s. readTextStrips (strips only) 2.58, 2.35, 2.35 s against 3.88, 3.45, 3.44 s. Texts, staves and boxes equal to texts.json on both, scores within the same 0.006, 0.002, 0.001. MusicXML byte-equal on all six runs. A tab that had run the bench's main-thread pipeline beforehand ran everything 5 to 10 times slower and was discarded.
result: Applied in MODEL_ROLES.

decision: Keep letters of any alphabet, apostrophes and hyphens in the title (cleanupText), and count any letter in isTempoMarking, instead of homr's a-z only.
why: homr's title_detection.cleanup_text replaces everything outside [a-zA-Z0-9] by a space, which mangles every non-English title, and is_tempo_marking counts only a-z letters, so a title in another alphabet is dropped as a tempo marking. The OCR alphabet itself carries the accents.
evidence: AbcMusicStudio read a Québec page's title as "Marche des l ves"; the PP-OCRv6 rec model's character metadata (18 708 entries) contains é, è, ê, à, ç, ù, ô, î and É. The three golden titles are a-z only (The Kesh, Grand Staff Study, CHORD STUDY) and unchanged.
result: Applied as a documented difference from homr (README, What this reproduces). Pinned with plain strings in test/title-text.test.ts; no page of the published score is committed.

decision: The tab guard paints each tab system white (its rows from 0.75 line spacing above the top line to 0.75 below the bottom one, one spacing wider than its lines) in the page homr reads, rather than dropping homr's staves that overlap a tab and their notes from the MusicXML.
why: homr reads a tab's lines as a staff, and a staff with its tab underneath as a piano grand staff whose bass staff is the tab. Painting the tab out before segmentation lets homr's own staff detection and transformer run unchanged on what is left; filtering afterwards would have to split a grand staff's MusicXML part and could not give the treble staff back its own crop.
evidence: Library recognizePage, Node, wasm, ocr false, sketch pages at 300 dpi. Cripple Creek with score: before 4 grand staves (h 0.134 to 0.136), 382 pitched notes of which 187 on staff 2; after 4 staves (h 0.028 to 0.036), 168 pitched, none on staff 2. Against the tab's 169 pitch events: before 129 exact and 152 sharing a note (staff 1 only), after 117 and 143; the treble is read from a single-staff crop now and homr misreads it differently (the B4 of the B4 C#5 figure goes missing), with no run of invented rests. Arkansas Traveler and Kildare: homr never took their 4-line tabs for staves; 4 staves and 115 and 135 pitched notes before and after, pitch agreement with the tab unchanged (115/115, 3/21), but the rhythm moves (divisions 4 to 2, 6 to 12, one more measure on Kildare) because the painted page autocrops differently. The five tab-only PDFs: tablature_only.
result: Applied in src/pipeline/recognize.ts (TAB_MARGIN) and src/tab/detect.ts (whitenTablature). homr's port is untouched; a page without a tab is passed through as the same object, so the golden pages are byte-for-byte unaffected.

decision: tablature_only is answered when homr, run on the painted page, finds no staff or notehead (its not_music) and the guard found at least one tab; not from the detector's own count of five-line staves.
why: The detector is tuned to find tabs, not staves: on the Kildare scan it finds 2 of the 4 standard staves, so "no staff found by the detector" would refuse a page homr reads. Letting homr decide costs its segmentation on a tab-only page (28 to 36 s in Node) but never refuses music.
evidence: The five tab-only PDFs answer tablature_only after 28 to 36 s; the three staff-plus-tab PDFs answer ok with 4 staves each.
result: Applied in recognizePage's catch.

decision: A five-line group is classified from a sample of at most 12 of its line-sitting marks, read 6 at a time, stopping when the share read so far decides (tab: at least 4 numbers making at least half; staff: fewer than half numbers); a group with fewer than 4 digit-sized marks is a staff without reading anything.
why: The prototype read every mark and judged the share over all of them: 84 to 138 crops a tab page, 3 to 16 s in Node. The shares it measured (0.87 to 1.00 on tabs, 0.00 on staves) are far from the threshold, so a sample settles the same question. Noteheads are wider than a line space and never become marks, so a page of ordinary staves never opens the recogniser, which keeps the model-opening order the golden tests pin.
evidence: Library detector, the eight PDFs: 30/30 tab systems with their line counts, as the prototype; one recogniser run per five-line tab, 6 crops each (Cold Frosty Morning 84 crops to 36, 6.7 s to 3.1 s; Cripple Creek 138 to 24, 15.9 s to 2.2 s, first model open included). The three golden pages: 0 tabs, 0 recogniser calls, 0.2 to 0.3 s.
result: Applied in src/tab/detect.ts (marksAreNumbers, sampleOf). connectedComponentsWithStats joins REQUIRED_MEMBERS.

decision: Results gain tablature: TabSystem[] (index, lines 4 to 6, cx, cy, w, h page-normalised over the lines' extent), and RECOGNIZE_ERRORS gains tablature_only; RecognizeFailure becomes a union in which only tablature_only carries systems, always at least one. Version 0.3.0.
why: The app has to tell "this page is tablature" from "this page is not music" and show where the tabs are. The field is browser-only: the AbcGoDb server's OmrRecognizeResult has no tab guard. A new error code is a compile break for a consumer with an exhaustive Record over RecognizeError, and a new required field breaks object literals typed as a result, hence the minor version.
evidence: The AbcMusicStudio app (main, uncommitted, 2026-10-08) already keys RECOGNIZE_REFUSALS on RecognizeError | "tablature_only" and reads tablature with a runtime guard; its test helper failure(error: RecognizeError) builds a failure without tablature and needs tablature: [] and the narrower error type under 0.3.0.
result: Applied in src/result.ts, src/index.ts (TabSystem exported), README, package.json 0.3.0. src/version.ts holds homr's version, not the package's, and is unchanged. Not published.

decision: Two line-grouping rules beyond the prototype's: every line of a group overlaps the group's first line over 0.6 of the wider of the two (the prototype: 0.5 of the first), and no line of a group breaks for more than 5 line spacings (longest run of columns with no ink on the line's rows).
why: The owner's three guitar PDFs (TablEdit-like, Guitar Pro-like and DADGADTabs) brought two false tabs the eight banjo and mandolin pages never showed: a row of chord diagrams, whose fret rows line up across the diagrams into six evenly spaced short "lines", and a 16th-note beam above a staff that joined its five lines into a six-line group. The beam is a third of the staff's width; the diagrams' fret rows break for a dozen spacings between diagrams, where a fret number's knock-out is about one.
evidence: Library detector, 15 pages: before the rules 30/30 on the banjo and mandolin pages but 34 for 26 on the guitar pages (Amazing Grace 3/2, 4/3, 6/3; Moon over Shanghai 6/5 twice). A 0.8 overlap share lost the third Chicken reel tab, whose top line's long runs start at x 259 of 76 (dense numbers). After: 56/56 with the right line counts, the golden pages still 0 tabs and 0 recogniser calls.
result: Applied in src/tab/detect.ts (minOverlap, maxBreak, PageLine.breakLength); test/tab-local.test.ts holds the 15-page truth.

decision: Painting tabs out holds on the guitar pages too, so it stays the guard's one mechanism.
why: The first row's choice was measured on banjo and mandolin pages only; the owner's guitar PDFs put a 6-line tab under one or two standard staves, the layout most guitar books use.
evidence: homr before (HEAD) and after, Node, wasm, ocr false, 300 dpi. Amazing Grace p1/p2/p3 (voice and guitar staves over each tab): before 4/6/6 staves, the tabs read as staves of h 0.035 to 0.047 next to homr's voice-plus-guitar grand staves (h 0.150 to 0.158), 106/128/156 pitched notes; after 2/3/3 grand staves, 0 on a tab, 91/112/127 pitched. Moon over Shanghai p1/p2/p3: before 4/5/5 staves, most boxes h 0.099 to 0.114 (staff and tab taken as one), 1/2/4 notes on a second staff; after all h 0.020 to 0.022, none on a second staff, 178 to 182, 237 to 235, 173 to 160 pitched. Brian Boru's March (DADGAD): before 4 boxes of h 0.104 over staff and tab, after h 0.026; the first two systems' pitches are the same but for one F4 read as F#4 after, which the key signature (D) makes right.
result: No code change; recorded so the guitar evidence sits beside the banjo evidence.

decision: The reader is the guard's own connected-component pass carried to the end (src/tab/read.ts over marksOf/cropOf/readFret exported from src/tab/detect.ts), run inside recognizePage right after detection and before homr, on every tab the guard found; RecognizeSuccess.tablature and the tablature_only failure carry TabReading (TabSystem plus events, annotations, unread) instead of TabSystem.
why: One mark finder for both means the guard and the reader can never disagree on what sits on a line, and the prototype measured exactly this pipeline. Reading before homr puts the frets on a tablature_only failure too, which is the page where they matter most. TabReading extends TabSystem, so a consumer typed on TabSystem keeps compiling.
evidence: Local accuracy script (tools/tab-accuracy.ts) on the prototype's rasters (byte-identical PNGs): every figure of .scratch/tab-sketch/REPORT.md reproduced (see the other tab-2 rows).
result: Applied in src/tab/read.ts, src/pipeline/recognize.ts, src/result.ts, src/index.ts, src/internal.ts. homr's port untouched; a page without a tab never calls the reader.

decision: An event is { x, notes: [{ string, fret }, ...] } with at least one note, one per string, ordered by string; not { x, string, fret, chord }.
why: A primary note plus a chord list repeats one fret in two places and lets them disagree. A non-empty tuple with a single-note chord for a lone note has one representation per event. eventsOf adds a guard the prototype lacked: a second fret on a string already in the open event starts a new event.
evidence: Unit tests on eventsOf; local pages unchanged by the guard (169 events on both Cripple Creek pages, as the prototype).
result: Applied in src/tab/read.ts (TabEvent, TabNote, eventsOf).

decision: Technique letters are a table of recogniser reads to eight tokens (Sl, Po, H, R, p, h, x, Harm.), tried before a fret; they come out as annotations { x, string, technique } beside the events, and marks that read as neither are counted in unread.
why: Tried after a fret, "Po" read as P stuck to an O, which the fret rule turns into a 0: a note that is not there. TablEdit's Sl and Po often reach the recogniser as the capital alone, since the second letter is x-height. The count keeps the TAB clef and time signatures visible without inventing tokens for them.
evidence: Cripple Creek tab-only: Sl 12, Po 6, H 1, unread 2 (the prototype: 15 unread marks, P and S among them); with score: Sl 13, Po 6, H 1; Sourwood Mountain: Po 6, H 1, Sl 2; Cold Frosty Morning unread 12 (its TAB clef). Typeset fixtures: every letter on its string.
result: Applied in src/tab/read.ts (TECHNIQUE_READS, readMark).

decision: Marks under 0.75 of the median height are no longer dropped by the reader: they are read in a second recogniser call and count only as technique letters; a tall letter followed within 0.35 spacing by short letters on its line is read as one word (H + ar = Harm.).
why: The height cut exists to drop pull-off arcs cut by a stem, but it also dropped an x-height x (0.68 of the digit height in TeX Gyre Bonum) and split Harm. into H and a short tail. Accepting only a technique from a short mark keeps arcs out of the events and out of unread.
evidence: Typeset guitar page: x and Harm. read only with the rule. It cannot change an event: a short mark yields an annotation or nothing, and joining extends only marks read as letters.
result: Applied in src/tab/read.ts (joinWords, readingOf). marksOf returns { marks, short }; the guard uses marks only, as before.

decision: Line erasure keeps a short horizontal run held by a stroke at both ends: a line pixel is erased only when nothing touches the line there from above or below and the pixel lies in a run at least one spacing long or with a free end.
why: The bar of an H standing on the line inside a knock-out was erased as line, splitting the H into two marks read "I" "I". A rule on run length alone (at least one spacing) kept the line stubs left beside TablEdit's knock-outs glued to the digits and cost Cripple Creek 3 events and 13 notes; the free-end rule keeps every local page's marks as before.
evidence: Marks before and after on the 15 local pages: identical but for 41 marks of Sourwood Mountain one pixel wider. Typeset banjo page: H read only with the rule. The guard's 56/56 tab-local test holds.
result: Applied in src/tab/detect.ts (bandWithoutLines, ruledColumns); shared by the guard.

decision: A mark the line runs into from both sides (a number printed without a knock-out) is cropped from the line-erased ink; a knocked-out mark keeps its own ink.
why: The recogniser reads 12 with a line through it as 2. Cropping every mark from erased ink fixed that but took the middle bar of digits held on one side only (3, 5) where TablEdit's knock-outs leave the line touching them: Cripple Creek fell from 202 to 198 notes and its consistency from 161 to 157.
evidence: Typeset mandolin system without knock-outs: 12 read twice only with erased crops. Local pages with the both-sides rule: the prototype's figures exactly.
result: Applied in src/tab/read.ts (struck, withoutLines).

decision: The digit merge gap stays the prototype's 0.18 spacing.
why: Opencv's Hershey digits in the guard's synthetic page stand 4 to 8 px apart at 150 dpi, so its 10, 11 and 12 read as two frets. A gap of 0.45 joined them and also joined neighbouring frets on TablEdit's dense Cripple Creek (166 events to 148 and consistency 156 to 135, everything else equal in that intermediate build); 0.3 did not join Hershey's 11. Real tab software sets the two digits touching, which the typeset fixtures cover.
evidence: Measured with tools/tab-accuracy.ts at 0.18, 0.3 and 0.45.
result: No change; test/tab-guard.test.ts checks the synthetic page's first seven columns, all single digits.

decision: Pitch is a separate pure function, pitchTab(reading, { strings, capo }): open string MIDI + capo + fret, strings top line first, the capo applied to every string including a banjo's fifth (the bottom line); midiOfPitch parses scientific names. Tuning and capo OCR is step 3.
why: The page prints tuning and capo as text the library does not read yet, so the caller supplies them. The prototype's Cripple Creek pitches matched the staff above with the fifth string taking capo 2.
evidence: Unit tests (banjo open G, capo 0 and 2); the local script's staff comparison runs through pitchTab: Arkansas Traveler 115/115.
result: Applied in src/tab/pitch.ts; exported from homr-web.

decision: Committed fixtures are three A4 pages at 300 dpi typeset by tools/typeset-tab.mjs (SVG built from column specs, rasterised by rsvg-convert, 8-bit grayscale PNG, 36 to 48 KB each) with truth.json written by the same run; tests load the PNGs.
why: Typeset with real fonts (Roboto, TeX Gyre Bonum) they are faithful to tab software in a way the Hershey drawing is not, and the truth comes from the layout that drew them. Committing PNGs keeps the test run free of rsvg and fonts; the generator is byte-identical from run to run on one machine.
evidence: 122 events over 7 systems (4, 5 and 6 lines), all read exactly, with every technique letter, the slur dropped and the TAB clef unread.
result: Applied in tools/typeset-tab.mjs, test/fixtures/tab/, test/tab-read.test.ts.

decision: Version 0.4.0, not published: tablature elements gain fields, PROGRESS_STAGES gains tab, and new exports (pitchTab, midiOfPitch, TAB_TECHNIQUES, the Tab* and Pitched* types).
why: A new progress stage breaks a consumer with an exhaustive Record over ProgressStage, and object literals typed as a result now need the reading fields, so a minor version.
evidence: npm run check and npm run lint clean.
result: Applied in package.json.

decision: TabReading gains optional tuning and capo, per system: tuning is a union on status (read and string_count carry strings, pitch names top line first, with source text or named; unknown_name carries the text only), capo is { fret, text, confidence }. Absent means the page says nothing; no default is ever filled in. Version stays 0.4.0.
why: pitchTab works on one reading and line counts live on the system; a margin label speaks for its system while a header speaks for every system, resolved against each system's own line count. A union keeps a tuning without strings or with the wrong count from reaching pitchTab as if it fitted. Optional fields change no existing field's meaning, so the unpublished 0.4.0 takes them; the tab progress stage's total gains one step for the text, also unpublished.
evidence: 23 local pages: 10 tunings and 5 capos printed, all read right, none invented on the 13 that print no tuning. Typeset header pages: string_count for DADGAD over five lines, unknown_name for Open Zeta.
result: Applied in src/tab/read.ts (TabReading), src/tab/tuning.ts (TabTuning, TabCapo), src/result.ts and src/index.ts exports.

decision: The parser is a table: compact letters, spaced letters, string assignments, names per string count (English and French), per-line margin labels, capo patterns; letters are read bottom line first and each takes the octave nearest the same string of the standard tuning for that string count. Spaced letters and names count only beside a tuning word or alone on their line.
why: Every page measured lists strings low to high, the bottom line first, a banjo's lowercase first letter being its fifth string, the bottom line; the Guitar Pro sample's MusicXML confirms line 1 (bottom) is G4. One registry per string count is what makes Open G DGDGBD on a guitar and gDGBD on a banjo. Without the tuning-word guard a title such as Jazz Standard would set standard tuning.
evidence: test/tab-tuning.test.ts, 77 cases: aEAC#E gives E4 C#4 A3 E3 A4, f#DF#AD D4 A3 F#3 D3 F#4, (6)=D drop D, Sawmill over six lines string_count; Jazz Standard, Key Of A, Clawhammer Banjo, TITMTITM and 12 other header strings give nothing.
result: Applied in src/tab/tuning.ts (parseTabText, parseLetterLabels, resolveTuning, standardStrings); midiOfPitch moved there from pitch.ts, exported from homr-web as before.

decision: The text is read in three kinds of region: the header (page top to 0.75 spacing above the first tab), the line under the first system (0.75 to 3.5 spacings below it), and each system's left margin (5 spacings above its top line, or the system above, to 1 below). A margin label holds for the systems after it until the next one. Ranking: fits the line count, from a margin, printed letters over a name, recogniser score.
why: Those are the four places the 23 pages print tuning and capo (header, over bar 1, margin turned a quarter, under the first system). A margin reach of 1 spacing cut Blackberry Blossom's score-and-tab label, which is centred on staff and tab together, between header and margin, and it was read in neither. Guitar Pro prints the label beside the first system only, so without persistence every later system had no tuning.
evidence: tools/tab-accuracy.ts --text: with reach 1, Blackberry Blossom tab and score missing; with 5, correct. Per-line labels and the under-system line covered by the typeset header pages.
result: Applied in src/tab/text.ts (regionsOf, speakingFor, rankOf).

decision: RapidOcr.read and trace take an optional detection limit (RapidOCR's Det.limit_type and limit_side_len), default min 736 as before; the tab text reads with max 1280.
why: The default brings the short side up to 736: a 2480 by 102 strip became about 18 000 by 736 and took 2.3 s with nothing on it. max 1280 keeps 300 dpi header text 20 px tall or more for the detector, and recognition still crops at RapidOCR's own scale.
evidence: 23 pages, Node, wasm: the same readings at 2000, 1280 and 960; text 2.4 to 7.2 s a page at 2000, 1.3 to 5.2 s at 1280, 1.0 to 3.5 s at 960. 960 leaves 14 px text, near the detector's floor, for 1 s.
result: Applied in src/ocr/rapid-ocr.ts (DetectionLimit, DEFAULT_DETECTION_LIMIT) and src/tab/text.ts (LIMIT). The chord strips and ocr-golden tests use the default and are unchanged.

decision: recognizePage reads the tab text right after the frets on every page with a tab, whatever the ocr option, opening the OCR detector and classifier; a failure logs and leaves the systems without tuning, a cancel cancels.
why: The tuning belongs to the tab reading, without which no fret has a pitch; ocr governs the chord strips and the title. Failing alone matches the chord strips. A page without a tab never reaches it, so the golden pages, their timings and model-opening order are untouched.
evidence: test/tab-guard.test.ts: the Hershey page (ocr false) answers tablature_only with no tuning and no capo, progress tab 1/3 to 3/3, and a Tab text log line.
result: Applied in src/pipeline/recognize.ts (readTabTextOrNothing, describeTabText).

decision: pitchTab(reading) without a tuning uses the read tuning and capo (no printed capo is capo 0) and throws when no fitting tuning was read; a tuning passed in wins. tuningOf(reading) and standardTuning(lines) are exported.
why: The read value has to be usable directly, and correctable: the app shows text and confidence and passes the musician's correction. Applying the standard tuning is a caller's decision, so it is a helper, never a fallback.
evidence: test/tab-pitch.test.ts: Sawmill with capo 2 gives A4 on the fifth string; standardTuning(5) passed in gives G4; no tuning throws naming standardTuning(5); unknown_name gives no tuningOf.
result: Applied in src/tab/pitch.ts.

decision: Eleven header pages added to tools/typeset-tab.mjs (HEADER_PAGES), full A4, one short system each, with truth.json's headers holding what each page's text says; the three fret pages unchanged byte for byte and used as the pages that print nothing.
why: The local pages hold only English banjo text in four layouts; French, guitar and mandolin text, Roman and ordinal capos, string assignments, per-line labels, a wrong string count and an unknown name need pages with known text. Shorter pages (900 px) found no tab: a line gap must be at most 3 % of the page height.
evidence: test/tab-text.test.ts: 14 of 14. Regenerated twice: all 15 files byte-identical. 29 to 36 KB a page, 360 KB in all.
result: Applied in tools/typeset-tab.mjs, test/fixtures/tab/, test/tab-text.test.ts.

decision: Finding: the prototype's ten pages print a tuning on five, not nine; and the guard takes staves for tabs on two Guitar Pro score-and-tab PDFs (Blackberry Blossom 5 tabs for 3, Old Joe Clark 7 for 4).
why: The prototype's typed tunings included ones taken from file names and assumptions (DADGAD photo, open G on Chicken reel). The false tabs are a staff whose top line the guard missed (read as four lines) and staves whose fingering digits read as frets; those PDFs were never in step 1's truth.
evidence: Pages viewed at 300 dpi; tools/tab-accuracy.ts --text tab counts.
result: Recorded in docs/design/tab-3-findings.md; the accuracy tool scores the systems' most common reading. The guard fix is left to a step-1 follow-up.
